expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: trialing has only trialEndsAt, active has only renewsAt, past_due has retryCount/gracePeriodEndsAt, canceled has canceledAt/cancellation

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: assertNever function defined and used in entitlementEndsAt switch with default case

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: function transition() that checks LEGAL_TRANSITIONS table and throws IllegalTransitionError on invalid transitions

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Table with 7 rows enumerating misuses and how each is made impossible: discriminated union, inaccessible until narrowed, cancellation union, branded types, assertNever, bounds checking, transition guard

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary design is discriminated union; opens by explicitly contrasting with problematic 6-optional-fields approach
